findings.title: Cleanup uses literal string "alias" instead of the actual IDP alias
findings.body: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, the cleanup registration `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` uses the literal string `"alias"` instead of the actual alias `"idp-alias-" + i`. This means the cleanup will attempt to look up a non-existent IDP with alias "alias" and will never actually remove the 20 IDPs created in the loop. This can cause test pollution, affecting subsequent tests that assume a clean realm state. The same issue exists on line 425 for the additional IDP created in step 1.

findings.title: getForLogin cache does not check organization invalidation unlike getByOrganization
findings.body: The `getByOrganization` method (line 173) checks `isInvalid(cacheKey) || isInvalid(orgId)` before serving from cache, but `getForLogin` only checks `isInvalid(cacheKey)`. If an organization is invalidated (e.g., disabled), the login cache will still return the organization's IDPs. The `isEnabled()` re-check added in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` mitigates this for the login page, but any other caller of `getForLogin` that does not re-check `isEnabled()` could receive IDPs from a disabled organization. Consider adding an `isInvalid(organizationId)` check similar to `getByOrganization`, or documenting that callers must always re-check `isEnabled()` on results.

findings.title: registerIDPLoginInvalidation may silently skip invalidation when BROKER_PUBLIC is toggled on an org-linked IDP via create
findings.body: In `registerIDPLoginInvalidation`, the predicate `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)` includes the check `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`. If an IDP is created with `organizationId` set but `BROKER_PUBLIC` not yet in config (e.g., it will be set in a subsequent update), the predicate returns false and the login cache is not invalidated on creation. While the subsequent update would trigger invalidation via `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate`, there is a brief window where the cache is stale. This is a minor concern since the typical flow sets all config at creation time, but worth noting for correctness.
